questions.stem: Consider a parallel plate capacitor of area $A$ (of each plate) and separation $d$ between the plates. If $E$ is the electric field and $\epsilon_0$ is the permittivity of free space between the plates, then potential energy stored in the capacitor is :-
questions.solution:
$\frac{U}{V} = \frac{1}{2}\epsilon_0 E^{2}$
$U = \frac{1}{2}\epsilon_0 E^{2} V$
$= \frac{1}{2}\epsilon_0 E^{2}(Ad)$

questions.stem: What is the relative decrease in focal length of a lens for an increase in optical power by $0.1\ \mathrm{D}$ from $2.5\ \mathrm{D}$ ? ['D' stands for dioptre]
questions.solution:
When $P = 2.5\ \mathrm{D}$
$F = \frac{1}{P} = \frac{1}{2.5}$
When $P' = 2.6\ \mathrm{D}$
$F' = \frac{1}{P'} = \frac{1}{2.6}$
Relative decrease in focal length
$\frac{F - F'}{F} = \frac{\frac{2}{5} - \frac{5}{13}}{\frac{2}{5}} = 1 - \frac{25}{26} = \frac{1}{26} = 0.04$

questions.stem: An air bubble of radius $0.1\ \mathrm{cm}$ lies at a depth of $20\ \mathrm{cm}$ below the free surface of a liquid of density $1000\ \mathrm{kg/m^{3}}$. If the pressure inside the bubble is $2100\ \mathrm{N/m^{2}}$ greater than the atmospheric pressure, then the surface tension of the liquid in SI unit is (use $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^{2}}$)
questions.solution:
$T$ is surface tension
$P$ in air bubble $= P_0 + \rho g h + \frac{2T}{R}$
$P_{in} - P_0 = \rho g h + \frac{2T}{R} = 2100$
$\frac{2T}{R} = 2100 - \rho g h$
$T = \frac{R}{2}\left(2100 - 10^{3} \times 10 \times 0.2\right)$
$= \frac{1}{20}\left(2100 - 2000\right) \times 10^{-2}$
$= 0.05$

questions.stem: For an experimental expression $y = \frac{32.3 \times 1125}{27.4}$, where all the digits are significant. Then to report the value of $y$ we should write :-
questions.solution:
$y = \frac{32.3 \times 1125}{27.4} = 1326.186$
Last significant digits are 3 in operands so results should rounded off to 3 digits.
$\therefore y = 1330$

questions.stem: During the transition of electron from state A to state C of a Bohr atom, the wavelength of emitted radiation is $2000\ \mathrm{\AA}$ and it becomes $6000\ \mathrm{\AA}$ when the electron jumps from state B to state C. Then the wavelength of the radiation emitted during the transition of electrons from state A to state B is :-
questions.solution:
$E_A - E_C = \frac{hc}{2000\mathrm{\AA}}$ ..... (i)
and $E_B - E_C = \frac{hc}{6000\mathrm{\AA}}$ ..... (ii)
Now $E_A - E_B = (E_A - E_C) - (E_B - E_C)$
$\frac{hc}{\lambda_{AB}} = \frac{hc}{2000} - \frac{hc}{6000}$
$\frac{1}{\lambda_{AB}} = \frac{1}{3000\mathrm{\AA}}$
$\lambda_{AB} = 3000\mathrm{\AA}$

questions.stem: The amount of work done to break a big water drop of radius $R$ into 27 small drops of equal radius is $10\ \mathrm{J}$. The work done required to break the same big drop into 64 small drops of equal radius will be :-
questions.solution:
$W = \Delta U = S\Delta A$
One drop to $n$ drop
$\frac{4}{3}\pi R^{3} = n\frac{4}{3}\pi r^{3}$
$r = \frac{R}{n^{\frac{1}{3}}}$
So $W = S\left(n 4\pi r^{2} - 4\pi R^{2}\right)$
$= S 4\pi R^{2}\left(n^{\frac{1}{3}} - 1\right)$
For one drop to 27 drops
$W = S 4\pi R^{2}\left(27^{\frac{1}{3}} - 1\right) = 10$ ..... (i)
For one drop to 64 drops
$W' = S 4\pi R^{2}\left(64^{\frac{1}{3}} - 1\right)$ ... (ii)
(ii)/(i)
$\frac{W'}{W} = \frac{4 - 1}{3 - 1} = \frac{3}{2}$
$W' = \frac{3}{2}W = 155$

questions.stem: An object of mass $m$ is projected from origin in a vertical $xy$ plane at an angle $45^\circ$ with the $x$-axis with an initial velocity $v_0$. The magnitude and direction of the angular momentum of the object with respect to origin, when it reaches at the maximum height, will be [$g$ is acceleration due to gravity]
questions.solution:
$H = \frac{\left(\frac{v_0}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{2}}{2g} = \frac{v_0^{2}}{4g}$
$L = mvh$
$L = m\frac{v_0}{\sqrt{2}}\frac{v_0^{2}}{4g}$

questions.stem: The Young's double slit interference experiment is performed using light consisting of 480 nm and 600 nm wavelengths to form interference patterns. The least number of bright fringes of 480 nm light that are required for the first coincidence with the bright fringes formed by 600 nm light is :-
questions.solution:
$\frac{n_1\lambda_1 D}{d} = \frac{n_2\lambda_2 D}{d}$
$n\, 480 = m\, 600$
$n_{min} = 5$

questions.stem: A car of mass $m$ moves on a banked road having radius $r$ and banking angle $\theta$. To avoid slipping from banked road, the maximum permissible speed of the car is $v_0$. The coefficient of friction $\mu$ between the wheels of the car and the banked road is :-
questions.solution:
$N\sin\theta + f\cos\theta = \frac{mv^{2}}{R}$
$N\cos\theta - f\sin\theta = mg$
$\frac{\sin\theta + \mu\cos\theta}{\cos\theta - \mu\sin\theta} = \frac{v^{2}}{Rg}$
$Rg\tan\theta + \mu Rg = v^{2} - v^{2}\mu\tan\theta$
$\mu = \frac{v^{2} - Rg\tan\theta}{Rg + v^{2}\tan\theta}$

questions.stem: A uniform solid cylinder of mass $m$ and radius $r$ rolls along an inclined rough plane of inclination $45^\circ$. If it starts to roll from rest from the top of the plane then the linear acceleration of the cylinder axis will be :-
questions.solution:
$a = \frac{g\sin\theta}{1 + \frac{I}{mR^{2}}}$
$a = \frac{\frac{g}{\sqrt{2}}}{1 + \frac{1}{2}} = \frac{2}{3}\frac{g}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{\sqrt{2}g}{3}$

questions.stem: A thin plano convex lens made of glass of refractive index 1.5 is immersed in a liquid of refractive index 1.2. When the plane side of the lens is silver coated for complete reflection, the lens immersed in the liquid behaves like a concave mirror of focal length $0.2\ \mathrm{m}$. The radius of curvature of the curved surface of the lens is :-
questions.solution:
$\frac{1.5}{v} = \frac{1.5 - 1.2}{R}$
$v = \frac{1.5R}{0.3} = 5R$
$\frac{1.2}{f} - \frac{1.5}{5R} = \frac{1.2 - 1.5}{-R}$
$\frac{1.2}{f} = \frac{0.3}{R} \times 2 \Rightarrow f = 2R \Rightarrow R = 0.1$

questions.stem: A particle is executing simple harmonic motion with time period $2\ \mathrm{s}$ and amplitude $1\ \mathrm{cm}$. If $D$ and $d$ are the total distance and displacement covered by the particle in $12.5\ \mathrm{s}$, then $\frac{D}{d}$ is :-
questions.solution:
$A = 1\ \mathrm{cm}$
$n = \frac{12.5}{2} = 6.25\ \mathrm{cycles}$
$\therefore D = 4 \times 6 + 1 = 25$
$d = 1$
$\frac{D}{d} = 25$

questions.stem: A satellite is launched into a circular orbit of radius $R$ around the earth. A second statellite is launched into an orbit of radius $1.03\ R$. The time period of revolution of the second satellite is larger than the first one approximately by :-
questions.solution:
$T^{2} = KR^{3}$
$\frac{2\Delta T}{T} = \frac{3\Delta R}{R}$
$\frac{2\Delta T}{T} = \frac{3 \times 0.03R}{R}$
$\frac{\Delta T}{T} = \frac{3 \times 0.03}{2} \times 100 = 4.5\%$

Another plano-convex lens with first surface radius of curvature of $3\ \mathrm{cm}$ has focal length of $f_2$ when it is immersed in a liquid of refractive index 1.2. If both the lenses are made of same glass of refractive index 1.5, the ratio of $f_1$ and $f_2$ will be :-

An alternating current is given by
$I = I_A \sin\omega t + I_B \cos\omega t$.
The r.m.s. current will be :-
questions.solution:

questions.stem: An electron of mass $m$ with an initial velocity $\vec{v} = v_0\hat{i}\ (v_0 > 0)$ enters an electric field $\vec{E} = -E_0\hat{k}$. If the initial de Broglie wavelength is $\lambda_0$, the value after time $t$ would be :-

A parallel plate capacitor was made with two rectangular plates, each with a length of $l = 3\ \mathrm{cm}$ and breath of $b = 1\ \mathrm{cm}$. The distance between the plates is $3\ \mu\mathrm{m}$. Out of the following, which are the ways to increase the capacitance by a factor of 10 ?
A. $l = 30\ \mathrm{cm}$, $b = 1\ \mathrm{cm}$, $d = 1\ \mu\mathrm{m}$
B. $l = 3\ \mathrm{cm}$, $b = 1\ \mathrm{cm}$, $d = 30\ \mu\mathrm{m}$
C. $l = 6\ \mathrm{cm}$, $b = 5\ \mathrm{cm}$, $d = 3\ \mu\mathrm{m}$
D. $l = 1\ \mathrm{cm}$, $b = 1\ \mathrm{cm}$, $d = 10\ \mu\mathrm{m}$
E. $l = 5\ \mathrm{cm}$, $b = 2\ \mathrm{cm}$, $d = 1\ \mu\mathrm{m}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
$C = \frac{A\epsilon_0}{d}$
A : plate area
d : distance between the plates.
Capacitance initial
$= \frac{\epsilon_0 \, l b}{d} = \epsilon_0$ units
Option 'C'  $l = 6\ \mathrm{cm}$
$b = 5\ \mathrm{cm}$
$d = 3\ \mathrm{cm}$
Capacitance $= 10\ \epsilon_0$ units
Option 'E'  $l = 5\ \mathrm{cm}$
$b = 2\ \mathrm{cm}$
$d = 1\ \mathrm{cm}$
Capacitance $= 10\ \epsilon_0$ units
$\therefore$ Ans is option (1)

questions.stem: A force $F = \alpha + \beta x^{2}$ acts on an object in the $x$-direction. The work done by the force is $5\mathrm{J}$ when the object is displaced by $1\ \mathrm{m}$. If the constant $\alpha = 1\mathrm{N}$ then $\beta$ will be
questions.solution:
$F = \alpha + \beta x^{2}$
Work done $= \int F dx$
$5 = \int \left(\alpha + \beta x^{2}\right)dx$
$5 = \left.\alpha x + \frac{\beta x^{3}}{3}\right|_0^1$
$5 = \alpha + \frac{\beta}{3}\ [\alpha = 1]$
$4 = \frac{\beta}{3} \Rightarrow \beta = 12\ \mathrm{N/m^{2}}$

questions.stem:
An ideal gas goes from an initial state to final state. During the process, the pressure of gas increases linearly with temperature.
A. The work done by gas during the process is zero.
B. The heat added to gas is different from change in its internal energy.
C. The volume of the gas is increased.
D. The internal energy of the gas is increased.
E. The process is isochoric (constant volume process)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :-
questions.solution:
Given that
$P = kT$
$\frac{P}{T}$ = constant
$\therefore$ Volume is constant or isochoric process.
$\therefore W_D = 0$
$\therefore Q = \Delta U$
Also temperature increases hence internal energy increases.

questions.stem: The least count of a screw guage is $0.01\ \mathrm{mm}$. If the pitch is increased by 75% and number of divisions on the circular scale is reduced by 50%, the new least count will be _____ $\times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{mm}$.
questions.solution:
Given least count of Screw Gauge $= 0.01\ \mathrm{mm}$
$\mathrm{L.C} = \frac{(\mathrm{pitch})}{\mathrm{No.\ of\ circular\ turn}} = \frac{P}{N} = 0.01\ \mathrm{mm}$
New pitch $= \frac{P(1 + 0.75)}{N(1 - 0.5)} = \frac{P}{N}\left[\frac{1.75}{0.5}\right]$
$= (0.01)\, 3.5$
$= 0.035\ \mathrm{mm}$
$= 35 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{mm}$
$\therefore$ Ans. is 35

questions.stem: A wire of resistance $9\ \Omega$ is bent to form an equilateral triangle. Then the equivalent resistance across any two vertices will be __ohm.
questions.solution:
$9\ \Omega$ is the resistance of whole wire
$\therefore$ resistance of each wire $= 3\ \Omega$.
$\therefore$ Equivalent resistance $= 2\ \Omega$

questions.stem:
A current of $5\mathrm{A}$ exists in a square loop of side $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\ \mathrm{m}$. Then the magnitude of the magnetic field $B$ at the centre of the square loop will be $p \times 10^{-6}\ \mathrm{T}$. where, value of $p$ is ______.
[Take $\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\ \mathrm{T\,mA^{-1}}$].
questions.solution:
Let $B$ be the magnetic field due to single side
then $B = \frac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi d}\left(\sin\theta_1 + \sin\theta_2\right)$
$= \frac{10^{-7} \times 5 \times 2}{\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = 2 \times 10^{-6}$
$\therefore B_{net}$ at centre O $= 4B$
$= 8 \times 10^{-6}$
$\therefore P = 8$ Ans.

questions.stem: The temperature of 1 mole of an ideal monoatomic gas is increased by $50^\circ\mathrm{C}$ at constant pressure. The total heat added and change in internal energy are $E_1$ and $E_2$, respectively. If $\frac{E_1}{E_2} = \frac{x}{9}$ then the value of $x$ is _______.
questions.solution:
Given that process is isobaric $\Delta T = 50^\circ\mathrm{C}$
Q in isobaric process $= nC_p\Delta T = E_1$
$\Delta U$ in isobaric process $= nC_v\Delta T = E_2$
$\therefore \frac{E_1}{E_2} = \frac{C_P}{C_V} = \gamma$
Given, gas is monoatomic
$\therefore \gamma = 1 + \frac{2}{f} = 1 + \frac{2}{3} = \frac{5}{3}$
Now, as per question.
$\frac{5}{3} = \frac{x}{9}$
$x = 15$
